The majority of PvP mounts are rewards for PvPers who have collected at least 2,000 Honor. They move at the same speed as the level 40 Epic mounts, and similarly require a Riding Skill of 150 (Journeyman) in order to ride. The mounts are available for purchase in the Hall of Legends in Orgrimmar, or Champions' Hall in Stormwind. There are five choices of reward mounts, representing the available races on each faction's side. The mount you can choose is not dependent on reputation with any city. For example, a human with sufficient Marks of Honor may choose to ride a Reins of the Black War Tiger, regardless of reputation with Darnassus. PvP seasons or arena seasons are periods in which rated PvP combat may occur. Each season has its own name (i.e. season 13 is called Tyrannical) and rewards. A season usually starts one week after the release of a major patch and ends when a new major patch is released. These seasons also usually coincide with PvE seasons. While the length of time between seasons varies, there is a PvP season active most of the year. With the release of Burning Crusade Classic, seasons returned but they usually launched with the release of a new patch (or Phase). During a PvP season, players can join rated arenas and battlegrounds in order to obtain Conquest Points which can be used to buy powerful PvP gear.

The PvP Talents system, introduced in Battle for Azeroth, allows the player to choose from several PvP-oriented abilities to augment their character. Each character can choose up to three PvP talents. Its general concept originated with Legions honor talents system, and a number of PvP talents began as honor talents. Unlike honor talents, however, PvP talents are unlocked simply by leveling up and do not require the player to grind honor. PvP talents' effects are always active in PvP instances, such as battlegrounds and arenas; and always inactive in PvE instances, such as raids and dungeons. In the open world, PvP talents are active as long as War Mode is turned on. Because of this, PvP tal

PvP scaling is a PvP game mechanic introduced with Battle for Azeroth. It adjusts the damage dealt to enemy players as well as healing to friendly players while engaged in PvP combat to partially compensate for gear item level differences between players. It is only applied to players between levels 110 to 120 and is intended to reduce the power gains acquired from gear in PvP, but not completely negate it. It is applied in all PvP activities such as world PvP, arenas, battlegrounds and duels.

RNG is a game term that is an acronym for "random number generator". Random number generators (or, more correctly, [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudorandom_number_generator pseudorandom number generators]) are algorithms used in computing when an outcome needs to be as random as possible. A computer can't generate completely random numbers on its own, so it uses a complex algorithm designed to get as close to random as is practical. These algorithms are used in the game any time an event has a probability of happening - whether that be critical hits, the spread of weapon damage, procs such as Missile Barrage or Sudden Doom, or to determine which loot drops from a raid boss. Race is a term used in World of Warcraft to split various unique creatures into separate groups. Numerous races populate Azeroth including elves, trolls, human, orcs, gnomes, and murlocs, among many others. Many races can interbreed including humans, high elves, night elves, ogres, orcs, and draenei — producing offspring often called half-breeds. The Warcraft universe is inhabited by many sentient and sapient beings. These races speak many different languages, have different homelands and racial traits, and can pursue different classes. Distinct racial leaders (or faction leaders) for the first ten playable races in World of Warcraft acted as a PvP boss NPC in the capital city of that playable race's faction. World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King added the For the Horde! and For the Alliance! achievements, gained for killing each of the opponent faction's racial leaders. The gnomes and trolls, due to being added late in the core game's development, lacked distinct capitals and had much less involved racial leaders that did not count towards the achievements. The initial racial leaders were Thrall, Vol'jin, Cairne Bloodhoof, Sylvanas Windrunner, Magni Bronzebeard, Gelbin Mekkatorque, Bolvar Fordragon, and Tyrande Whisper

Raknahama Pi'Lenda is both a Caretaker of the Chalice and Coin in the region of Kul Tiras. She looks after the remaining artifacts of the Proudmoore Estate. She takes it personally that the Grand Admiral and his daughter Jaina left the island with the fleet — and several of the family's artifacts — and did not return. A skilled rogue who specializes in trap creation, Raknahama is one of the few Caretakers who serves on the advisory board for Logan Palimore as well; she teaches basic trap creation to new recruits when she has the time to make the trip from Kul Tiras to the Arathi Highlands. She is in her early thirties, and has a scarred face from a mishap with an acid trap in her youth.

Rakmar Sharpfang was a necrolyte under the command of the warlock Gul'dan during the Second War. He was the unofficial leader of the group of necromancers. When Gul'dan submitted to Orgrim Doomhammer he promised him command of a powerful set of allies of his creation to use against the Alliance of Lordaeron. When Rakmar repeatedly failed Gul'dan to produce such a creature, the old warlock came up with another way for Rakmar to serve. Rakmar was the first of the necrolytes slaughtered for the sake of using their energies to create the death knights.

It was written about the glorification of Diablo, the primary antagonist of the Diablo universe, to celebrate Blizzard's newly announced development of Diablo III. It is uncertain if the band will record a studio version of the song.

The Faithless sethrak have been cruel to him and his brood, inflicting scars on Rakjan himself and subjugating many of his fellow pterrordax to use as mounts. Rakjan's old acquaintance Vorrik travels to Rakjan's Peak to recruit the pterrordax's aid against Faithless, and Rakjan readily agrees. Rally Bigbombs is a goblin located in R&D in the Motherlode. He used to be Jastor Gallywix's chief weapons researcher before he took a huge payday to work for the Venture Company. As such, Jastor ordered his death. His explosives are empowered with :Azerite.
Raging Wind Elementals were air elementals located in Stormwind City during the Elemental Unrest.
Raking Ferocity was an Azerite trait available to Feral druids.
Raliq's Debt drops from Raliq the Drunk in the World's End Tavern in Shattrath City.
Raging Vesper Vortex is a runecarving power obtained from Memory of the Raging Vesper Vortex.

Ramstein the Gorger is an elite abomination living in the burning city of Stratholme under the command of the Scourge. Like all abominations he is not particularly intelligent, and relying on his sense of tactics is an exceptionally poor idea. He is fearless, tenacious, and resilient, capable of pressing his advantage in combat for hours without growing weary or weak. He is responsible for the death of thousands, including ranger lord Nathanos Marris. Marris, now undead and working for the Forsaken under the name Nathanos Blightcaller, wants Ramstein killed.

Randis, the Human Orphan, is a human child quest giver located in Cathedral Square in Stormwind City. He is available only during Children's Week. To summon the orphan, the adventurer gets a whistle from Orphan Matron Nightingale as part of the Children's Week quest.
Ramstein's Lightning Bolts is a Level 48 quality Trinket that improves Critical Strike. It has an on use ability that causes area of effect Nature damage, with a 5 minute cooldown.
Raluhi is a draenei Aldor mage trainer located at the Terrace of Light in Shattrath City.
The Ramkahen Badge of Valor is a quest reward from Escape From the Lost City.
Randah Songhorn is a tauren guild vendor found in Thunder Bluff. During the feast for the Highmountain tauren, she was trapped by the Void.

Ran'thos Lunastre was a prominent nightborne noble and former head of House Lunastre, residing within the nightborne capital city of Suramar. The father of Ly'leth and Anarys, Ran'thos would eventually die under unclear circumstances shortly before the beginning of the Nightfallen rebellion; Ly'leth seems to believe that his death was the result of his opposition to Grand Magistrix Elisande. A memorial dedicated to Ran'thos stands in the Lunastre Estate. His daughter Ly'leth would succeed him as head of the family, and would carry the values of her father with her as she ruled her house. Ram'Pag, the Treasure Worm, is a giant worm that burrows out of the ground to attack the player when they attempt to loot the Totally Safe Treasure Chest on the summit of Reflection Peak in Highmountain. After killing Ram'Pag, the Actually Safe Treasure Chest containing an Offering to Ram'Pag appears on the ground instead.
Ranger Wain is a draenei located at Trueshot Lodge in Highmountain.
Ramkahen Legionnaires are tol'vir located in Neferset City in Uldum. They are present during the Assault in Uldum. They can also be summoned by Stolen Ramkahen Banner.
Ramkahen Scouts are tol'vir located in Lost City of the Tol'vir.
Ramkahen Envoy is a tol'vir that briefly appears in Ramkahen in Uldum after completing The High Council's Decision.
Rancidus the Sewer Monster was an ooze who haunted the citizens of Dalaran. Archmage Khadgar asked the Hidden Path to protect the city, which led to them finding and killing Rancidus.
Ram Haunches drop from Stonetalon Rams in Stonetalon Mountains.
Ransacked Supplies are located in the Sunken Path and the Shattered River in Nazmir.

Rampant Transference is a runecarving power obtained from Memory of Rampant Transference.

In healing, a ramp is a process where healing buffs are applied at a precise timing, which leads into the potential for a large amount of burst healing. Usually a cast sequence is used to ensure exact and reliable timing of the application of these healing buffs and also generate some sort of buff extension. In some cases once the damage has been received from the boss, then a second cast sequence may be used to activate the healing of these buffs. Healing ramps are a key part of the Discipline priest, Mistweaver monk, Restoration druid and Preservation evoker playstyles. Raptors are a type of predatory dinosaurs and one of the most iconic beasts of the Warcraft universe. They can be found both in Azeroth and Outland, as well as . They are superb hunting beasts that can track prey over great distances and are often lethal to encounter when caught unawares. They hunt in packs.
Ravage is a druid Cat Form druid ability, learned at level 32. It is a sneak attack that does a lot of damage, but requires the druid to be in Prowl and behind the target.

A rare pet defines a pet that has a rare or unique skin (appearance). In this case, rare or unique means the skin is only possessed by one or a very few difficult to find or acquire mobs. Since pet stats have been normalized, every pet of a particular type (i.e. cat, boar, bear, etc.) will have exactly the same movement speed, health, and attack speed. Primarily pets of one type are all the same as far as stats go. Pets learns new ranks of abilities as they go up in level. For more pet details and information on taming pets, see Pet (Hunter). Raschal worked as a courier for the night elves of Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas. He was recently declared missing in action by Ginro Hearthkindle, when he went missing for about a week when he set out for Thalanaar and never showed up. He was located at the Writhing Deep, inside the hive. His subsequent whereabouts following the Cataclysm are unknown.

Rated battlegrounds consist of pre-made battleground teams in a 10v10 bracket. As the highest-level form of battleground play in the game, rated battlegrounds typically see fierce competition between highly organized teams, with personal and team ranking at stake. Rated battlegrounds feature tighter restrictions on items and abilities, as with Arena play. All included battlegrounds are also scaled to 10v10, changing the pace of some battles. Rated battlegrounds offer substantial rewards in the form of Conquest Points, and are a decent option for earning new gear. Rapier of the Gilnean Patriots is provided as an objective for The Battle for Gilneas City.
Rapid Renewal is a passive specialization ability for Holy priests, available at level 64.

Ras'an is a master Pet Tamer located on the eastern edge of Sporewind Lake in Zangarmarsh, just outside Sporeggar. It is surrounded by its three battle pets: Fungor, Glitterfly, and Tripod. Defeating Ras'an is required to complete the Taming Outland and Taming Azeroth achievements.
Raskha is a jungle troll flight master located at Bambala in Northern Stranglethorn. During the events of war against the Zandalari, he was poisoned.

Ravager wasps are the second stage of the ravager life cycle. They are very aggressive and can often be found in swarms near their nests. Ravagers hatch as small ravenous larva, but soon disappear into pupae, only to emerge as slender wasps with a swarm mentality and a ferocious sting. Wasps quickly set out to gorge themselves until their wings can no longer support their body weight, after which they undergo a third and final metamorphosis into a vicious four-legged insect. Amberbarb wasps often try to provoke larger creatures to attack it. Once their victim strikes them, they will retaliate with the entire hive. The venom Gorgrond wasps have is extremely powerful. __NOTOC__ Rath'thul Moonvale is a blood elf quest giver and vendor that can show up at the Town Hall of the Horde Tier 3 garrison in Frostwall. He trades Primal Spirits for Draenic Dust and specialty patterns intended for enchanters.
Raukous is a wildkin located in Dalaran. He is accompanied by Moonkin Hatchlings.
__NOTOC__ Rauen Moontear is a night elf located at Valaar's Berth in the Azuremyst Isle. Since Elune's Blessing is out of commission, he created a mage portal to Darnassus to compensate.
Ratwhisker Luckydos are sold for by Bump-On-A-Log and Stick-In-The-Mud during Island Expeditions.

Rastari Defenders are Zandalari trolls located in Warport Rastari in Zuldazar. When the traitorous prophet Zul and Mythrax attacked the city, several of them were found dead. King Rastakhan asked Bwonsamdi for aid, and the Loa of Death raised the fallen defenders as Rastari Spirits.
The Rastari Bracers are a quest reward from Show of Strength.

The Rastari Skull Whistle is provided as an objective for No Troll Left Behind and Rally the Rastari. Given by Habutu, the Horde Speaker used it to rally Rastari Defenders in Warport Rastari. While not provided, it is also used during Show of Strength on Spirit Obelisks to summon Vengeful Ancestors from the Other Side, having been blessed with voodoo by Kaza'jin the Wavebinder.

The Ravager Cage Key is an item used to release the Death Ravager from the Ravager Cage in northern Azuremyst Isle. It is dropped by the Ravager Specimens that roam the Menagerie Wreckage. It's also provided for the warrior-only quest :Strength of One. This key is not consumed on use.
The Rappel Point is located on a Fel Tree Branch at the Moonlight Ascent on the Broken Shore.
Rat-Corpse Bag is an anima power obtained from anima caches in Torghast, Tower of the Damned.
Rattle the Stars is a Balance druid talent. It is an exclusive choice node with Starweaver.

Raynewood Retreat is located in north-central Ashenvale, around the Great Tree of the same name, east of Shael'dryn's moonwell and west of Night Run. It is an Alliance outpost where Ordanus, a keeper of the grove and one of the eldest sons of the forest god Cenarius, is hiding.
__NOTOC__ Raw Sagefish can be caught in Ashenvale, Hillsbrad Foothills, Loch Modan, Silverpine Forest and Stonetalon Mountains.
Ravenholdt Guards are human quest givers located in and around Ravenholdt Manor in the Hillsbrad Foothills and Alterac Mountains.

Raytaf was located on an island southeast of Hetaera's Clutch in Azshara. It was the pet of Loramus Thalipedes, along with Shahiar and Zaman.
Ravenous Oceanic Broadheads are hammerhead sharks swimming on Tranquil Wash in Shimmering Expanse.

Ravika is the quartermaster for the Darkspear Rebellion. She briefly appears at the Dranosh'ar Blockade near Fo'rum the Postmaker for players who are on To Be Prepared (Horde) and The Battle for Broken Shore (Horde) and have not yet been to the Broken Shore, and later takes up residence at Darkspear Hold within the Echo Isles.
The Ravenous Flayer Matriarch is a rock flayer located at the Coilskar Point in Shadowmoon Valley.
Raxx is a hell hound located in the Vault of the Wardens. It can be briefly seen during the demon hunter starting experience.

Razik Gazbolt is a goblin engineer and member of Hemet's Hunting Party found at Icepine Point in Highmountain. He is Hemet Nesingwary's munitions expert and is currently working on a prototype of a new project in the form of the Critter Hand Cannon. Lorna Stoutfoot disapproves of him, saying that his contraptions are unreliable at best and that a true hunter doesn't need gadgets to hunt. Razik has an assistant named Gertie.
Rax Sixtrigger is a goblin located at Talonrest in Stormheim. Along with his brother they killed friendly Highmountain tauren.
Raw Meat drops from Spinetusk Piglets at Cliff's Edge in Highmountain while on the quest Survive the Night.

Ravenous Sandworms are worms that can spawn upon using the Sandfishing ability in the Eastern Dunes in Vol'dun during the world quest Sandfishing. According to Kiro, sandworms are dangerous and savage predators that lurk beneath the dunes, but their fangs are valuable.

__NOTOC__ .]] Ravnyr is a dead dragon located in the Darkmaul Citadel on Exile's Reach. Gor'groth has tasked his ogres, as well as the island's quilboar and harpies, with harvesting enough life force to complete a ritual that will raise Ravnyr into undeath. Ultimately, Gor'groth gives himself as the final sacrifice to revive her.
The Ravenous Mite is a devourer located in the Endmire in Revendreth. It can be found flying around with Cudgelface in its clutches.
__NOTOC__ Ravenous Destroyers are devourers located in Ardenweald.
Razelikh's Defilement is a runecarving power obtained from Memory of Razelikh's Defilement.

Razorgore the Untamed is a dragonspawn of the black dragonflight and the first boss of Blackwing Lair. He has been tasked by the lord of Blackwing Lair, Nefarian, with guarding the numerous and precious black dragon eggs located in the first room of the instance. To this end, Razergore has been given command of a cohort of orcs and other forces, and will stop at nothing to ensure that no harm comes to his grave charges.

]] The Razormane Grounds, located in central Durotar, are the front lines of the battle for the Razormane quilboars' expansion from the Barrens into Durotar. Bones of dead animals stripped of their flesh litter the grounds, and brambles burst out of the red mountains high above. The orcs fight to keep the Razormane out of the orcish homeland, but for every one cut down, two seem to emerge from the thickets. Even after the Cataclysm, they have survived, thriving in the wake of the destruction. The leaders of this quilboar encampment are Geolord Mottle and Captain Flat Tusk, captain of the Battleguard.
The Razzashi Coin is a Paragon of Power sought after by the Zandalar Tribe.
Razor Gauntlets are plate gauntlets that give a bonus to strength as well as deals Arcane damage to melee attackers.
Razzeric is a goblin quest giver located at the Fizzle and Pozzik's Speedbarge in Thousand Needles. Before the Shattering, Razzeric was an independent goblin in Mirage Raceway.
__NOTOC__ Razortalon is a rare moonkin found in the Hinterlands.

__NOTOC__ Razormaw is an undead black dragon that haunts Wyrmscar Island off the coast of Bloodmyst Isle. He is summoned by using the Bundle of Dragon Bones, provided by Prince Toreth, on the Ever-burning Pyre.
Razorthorn Shelf is a passage between southwestern Hellfire Peninsula and northeastern Terokkar Forest. Inhabited by ravagers, it is the shortest route from Hellfire Peninsula to Shattrath City.

Razormane Destroyer was a level 10 quilboar from Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne. He was the leader of a group of Razormane quilboar in Mulgore, near Thunder Bluff, during The Founding of Durotar. He was killed by Rexxar, Chen Stormstout, and Rokhan during their quest to rescue Baine Bloodhoof.
Razzie Coalwrench is a goblin vendor located in the Shrine of Two Moons in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

Ready for Raiding IV is an achievement earned from defeating Ranjit without taking damage from the listed abilities in Skyreach on Heroic difficulty. After earning this achievement, the "Ready for Raiding" buff is automatically applied, which causes player characters to /dance and /cheer whenever standing still. The buff lasts for 5 minutes and its description reads "You're so ready!"
Ready for Powerleveling is a collections achievement awarded for acquiring fifteen heirlooms in the heirlooms tab, the third in a series.
Ready for Raiding V is an achievement earned from defeating the Wrath of Azshara without taking damage from Magic or Frost Resonance in the Eye of Azshara on Mythic difficulty.

In the canceled Warcraft Adventures, razor-rats were rats that dwelt within the Alterac Mountains. Thrall found the rotting carcass of an unfortunate razor-rat that got killed by the tesla coils protecting the gnomish inventors' workshop in the region. He later used that very same carcass as a reagent for his Death and Decay spell.

Razzi the Shaper is an ethereal located at Tradewinds Market in Boralus. He can reforge Azerite gear, allowing you to choice the Azerite powers you want on that piece of gear again. Razzi's cost for reshaping an Azerite armor piece starts at and doubles every time an item is reforged. This cost will decay by around 25% on each weekly server reset. He resides in the same shop as transmogrifier Warpweaver Ezil and Master of Fate Tezran.
